question.text: The number of ways of selecting <math><mn>15</mn></math> teams from <math><mn>15</mn></math> men and <math><mn>15</mn></math> women, such that each team consists of a man and a woman is

solution.text: First team can be selected in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mo>(</mo><mn>15</mn></msup><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msup><mo>.</mo><mn>15</mn></msup><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></math> way, second in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mo>(</mo><mn>14</mn></msup><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msup><mo>.</mo><mn>14</mn></msup><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></math> way and so on. So, number of ways of selecting <math><mn>15</mn></math> teams <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>15</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>15</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>15</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfenced></math>
